boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified no-cost ways to gather, study, read, stream, and see art on campus or around San Rafael, with student-only conditions identified where applicable.

cards.title: Read and Sing at Little Penguins Story Time
cards.subtitle: Archbishop Alemany Library front steps
cards.notes: Bring friends to read, play, and sing on the library steps; check the university page before going in case the gathering moves indoors.
cards.short_summary: A recurring, all-ages story gathering on Dominican’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Dominican states that Little Penguins Story Time meets on the first and third Friday of each month and is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Community and Neighborhood Engagement
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; all ages are welcome. The page says gatherings move just inside the library doors when it rains.

cards.entity_name: Archbishop Alemany Library Quiet Study Spaces
cards.title: Settle In for a Quiet Study Session
cards.subtitle: Archbishop Alemany Library
cards.notes: Meet for focused work, then choose a quiet study area; consult the library’s posted hours before heading across campus.
cards.short_summary: A no-purchase study hang in Dominican’s campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes Archbishop Alemany Library as providing Dominican students with academic resources and quiet study spaces.
cards.source_title: The Archbishop Alemany Library
cards.access_notes: Available to Dominican students during posted library hours; using the quiet study spaces does not require a purchase or admission ticket.

cards.title: Share a Course-Reserve Reading Session
cards.subtitle: Free assigned readings for Dominican students
cards.notes: Look up the reserve assigned by your professor, meet classmates at the library, and compare notes without buying another copy.
cards.short_summary: A group reading session built around free course materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Dominican’s student-services page says print and electronic readings placed on course reserve by professors are available for free.
cards.source_title: Services for Students
cards.access_notes: For Dominican students using assigned course reserves; the university explicitly states that reserve materials are available for free.

cards.title: Wander Through Art Works Downtown
cards.subtitle: Four galleries and working studios on Fourth Street
cards.notes: Enter from any Fourth Street storefront, browse the galleries together, and leave purchases entirely optional during your visit.
cards.short_summary: A free daytime gallery outing in downtown San Rafael.
cards.evidence_claim: Art Works Downtown’s official visitor page lists its San Rafael address and operating schedule and explicitly states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit AWD — Art Works Downtown
cards.access_notes: Free public admission during posted gallery hours; viewing does not require a purchase. Check the official page for current hours.

cards.title: Join the 2nd Friday Art Walk
cards.subtitle: Downtown San Rafael galleries and open studios
cards.notes: Start at Art Works Downtown, follow the current venue map with friends, and browse participating galleries and studios at your pace.
cards.short_summary: A monthly evening circuit through downtown art venues.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Art Works Downtown page says the 2nd Friday Art Walk is free to the public and publishes a 2026 schedule for the monthly event.
cards.source_title: 2nd Friday Art Walk — Art Works Downtown
cards.access_notes: Free to the public on scheduled second Fridays. Check the official page’s current venue map and schedule before leaving.

cards.title: Compare Notes in Gallery 1337
cards.subtitle: Art Works Downtown’s Fourth Street gallery
cards.notes: Choose one work each to discuss, read the current exhibition text, and compare interpretations without needing to buy anything.
cards.short_summary: A focused, conversation-friendly stop inside Art Works Downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Art Works Downtown identifies Gallery 1337 as its main public-facing gallery, while the same official page states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Exhibit Space Rental — Art Works Downtown
cards.access_notes: Free admission during Art Works Downtown’s posted public hours; purchases are optional and not required to view the gallery.

cards.title: Explore the Underground Gallery
cards.subtitle: An intimate exhibition room at Art Works Downtown
cards.notes: Head downstairs with a friend, take in the current solo or group installation, and allow time to discuss the smaller-scale setting.
cards.short_summary: An intimate gallery room suited to a short shared art break.
cards.evidence_claim: Art Works Downtown’s official gallery page names the Underground Gallery as an exhibition space, and the page states admission is free.
cards.source_title: Exhibit Space Rental — Art Works Downtown
cards.access_notes: Free admission during the art center’s public hours; confirm current hours and exhibition information on the official site.

cards.title: Meet Around the Founders’ Gallery
cards.subtitle: Lower-level exhibition space at Art Works Downtown
cards.notes: Walk the broad lower-level room together, look for three-dimensional work, and use the open layout for an unhurried conversation.
cards.short_summary: A spacious lower-level setting for a free group gallery visit.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Art Works Downtown page identifies Founders’ Gallery as a lower-level exhibition space and states that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Exhibit Space Rental — Art Works Downtown
cards.access_notes: Free admission during posted public hours; no artwork or merchandise purchase is required to enter and browse.

cards.title: Follow a Series Through 1325 Donors’ Gallery
cards.subtitle: Street-level display space at Art Works Downtown
cards.notes: Move through the elongated gallery as a group, trace how a displayed series develops, and compare which pieces hold your attention.
cards.short_summary: A compact street-level gallery for viewing a connected series.
cards.evidence_claim: Art Works Downtown describes 1325 Donors’ Gallery as a street-level display space, and its official page states admission is free.
cards.source_title: Exhibit Space Rental — Art Works Downtown
cards.access_notes: Free admission during Art Works Downtown’s public hours; browsing the display does not require a purchase.

cards.entity_name: Marin County Free Library Online Library
cards.title: Host a Library-Powered Movie Hang
cards.subtitle: Kanopy and Hoopla with an eligible library card
cards.notes: Have an eligible cardholder choose an available title, gather for a screening, and verify the service’s residence restrictions first.
cards.short_summary: A no-rental-cost movie session using public-library streaming.
cards.evidence_claim: Marin County Free Library says cardholders can stream movies and television for free through Kanopy and Hoopla, subject to service eligibility.
cards.source_title: Online Library | Marin County Free Library
cards.access_notes: Free with an eligible Marin County Free Library card number and PIN; some online services have residence-based restrictions.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along downtown San Rafael corridors within the practical orbit of Dominican University of California.

cards.title: See the Recreated Mission Chapel
cards.subtitle: Fifth Avenue corridor — a documented California mission site
cards.notes: Walk west along Fifth Avenue to see the recreated chapel, then use the available self-guided tour to examine the historic site.
cards.short_summary: A Fifth Avenue stop centered on San Rafael’s namesake mission chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: Mission San Rafael Arcángel is a 1949 recreation of the original mission at 1104 Fifth Avenue, with self-guided tours available.
cards.source_title: Mission San Rafael Arcangel - Landmarks | Marin Convention & Visitors Bureau
cards.access_notes: The source lists visitor access Monday–Friday 6:30 a.m.–5 p.m., Saturday 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m., and Sunday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm before departure.

cards.title: Use the Reopened Downtown Library
cards.subtitle: E Street corridor — public reading and research space
cards.notes: Enter from E Street for books, study time, or a library program; check the branch calendar before choosing a visit window.
cards.short_summary: A restored Carnegie-era library building with current public services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Downtown Library at 1100 E Street reopened on August 4, 2025, after safety, accessibility, and infrastructure work.
cards.source_title: Downtown Library Renovation Project | San Rafael Public Library
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours are 10 a.m.–7 p.m. Monday–Wednesday and 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Thursday–Sunday.

cards.title: Walk the Falkirk Grounds
cards.subtitle: Mission Avenue corridor — Victorian architecture and gardens
cards.notes: Continue along Mission Avenue to view the 1888 mansion, formal grounds, sculpture garden, and rotating upstairs exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: An art-and-garden stop inside a preserved Queen Anne estate.
cards.evidence_claim: Falkirk Cultural Center at 1408 Mission Avenue occupies an 1888 Queen Anne mansion with formal grounds, a sculpture garden, and contemporary-art galleries.
cards.source_title: Falkirk Cultural Center - General Arts & Culture | Marin Convention & Visitors Bureau
cards.access_notes: The source lists Tuesday–Friday 1–4:30 p.m. and Saturday 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; galleries may close for private events, so check first.

cards.title: Read Marin History Through Objects
cards.subtitle: B Street corridor — the Marin History Museum’s historic home
cards.notes: Turn onto B Street for artifact-based exhibits inside the 1879 Gate House; consult the museum before planning research-library work.
cards.short_summary: A Victorian gate house now used to interpret Marin County history.
cards.evidence_claim: The 1879 Boyd Gate House at 1125 B Street is home to the Marin History Museum and hosts exhibits and monthly tours.
cards.source_title: Visit | Marin History Museum
cards.access_notes: The museum posts Wednesday–Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–3 p.m.; verify tour dates separately.

cards.title: Browse Four Downtown Galleries
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street corridor — galleries and working artist studios
cards.notes: Enter from Fourth Street and move through the public galleries and studio halls; review current exhibitions before setting out.
cards.short_summary: A multi-gallery arts complex embedded in a historic downtown building.
cards.evidence_claim: Art Works Downtown’s Fourth Street building contains four galleries, 27 artist studios, a ceramic center, and other arts organizations.
cards.source_title: About AWD | Art Works Downtown
cards.access_notes: The organization invites visitors to check current exhibitions; confirm public gallery hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center
cards.title: Catch an Independent Film
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street corridor — nonprofit cinema programming
cards.notes: Check the current Fourth Street schedule, choose an age-appropriate screening, and reserve enough time for posted previews or discussions.
cards.short_summary: A downtown cinema presenting current independent and repertory films.
cards.evidence_claim: The Christopher B. Smith Rafael Film Center operates at 1118 Fourth Street and publishes current screenings with showtimes and ticket prices.
cards.source_title: Mary Oliver: Saved by the Beauty of the World | Smith Rafael Film Center
cards.access_notes: Showtimes vary by film; consult the current program page and film rating before attending.

cards.title: Pause at the Water-Wall Plaza
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street corridor — civic gathering space
cards.notes: Use the plaza as a Fourth Street pause point and photograph the water-wall feature; check the city calendar for scheduled public events.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable civic plaza at the center of downtown’s main corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: San Rafael City Plaza is a downtown community gathering place with a water-wall fountain and seasonal public events.
cards.source_title: About San Rafael | Downtown San Rafael
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access may be affected by scheduled events or maintenance; check the city event calendar before a dedicated trip.

cards.title: Search the Used-Book Shelves
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street corridor — independent used-book browsing
cards.notes: Walk west on Fourth Street and browse the organized used-book collections; call ahead if you need a particular subject or edition.
cards.short_summary: A compact West End bookstore with tens of thousands of used items.
cards.evidence_claim: Rebound Bookstore operates at 1611 Fourth Street and states that it carries approximately 45,000 books, CDs, and DVDs.
cards.source_title: Rebound Bookstore
cards.access_notes: The store posts Monday–Saturday hours of 11 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday closure; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Pick Up Bread from a Century-Old Bakery
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street corridor — a working neighborhood bakery
cards.notes: Stop at the Fourth Street storefront during posted retail hours and choose from the bakery counter; arrive before the 5 p.m. close.
cards.short_summary: A longstanding San Rafael bakery with a directly accessible storefront.
cards.evidence_claim: Bordenave’s French Bread Bakery operates at 1512 Fourth Street and says it has supplied fresh bread around the Bay Area for over a century.
cards.source_title: Contact | Bordenave’s French Bread Bakery
cards.access_notes: Store hours are posted as 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Saturday, with Sunday closure.

cards.title: Examine Political Art as Primary Evidence
cards.subtitle: Fifth Avenue corridor — posters, paintings, and historical objects
cards.notes: Visit the Fifth Avenue gallery to compare propaganda techniques across countries; allow time to read the museum’s seven thematic sections.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit collection focused on how political imagery shapes public opinion.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of International Propaganda at 1000 Fifth Avenue exhibits political posters, paintings, sculptures, and objects organized around seven themes.
cards.source_title: Museum of International Propaganda
cards.access_notes: Current posted hours are Thursday–Friday 9:30 a.m.–6:30 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m.
